q-110750.name: Question 1
q-110750.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ by inspection.
q-110750.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{2}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{2}=1\cdot {a}_{1}+1\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{2}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is spanned by just $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}},{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}\}.
$$

Question 2

Consider the vectors a1=[31],a2=[22], and a3=[1−1]. Find a basis of S=Span{a1,a2,a3} by inspection.

a
 B={[22]}
b
 B={[31]}
c
 B={[1−1]}
d
 B={[31],[22],[1−1]}
e
 B={[22],[1−1]}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Remember that a basis of S is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans S.

From the given vectors, we can see that a1 is a linear combination of vectors a2 and a3:

a1=1⋅a2+1⋅a3

Consequently, the vector a1 can be removed from Span{a1,a2,a3} without changing the span. So S=Span{a1,a2,a3} is spanned by just {a2,a3}.

Lastly, note that a2 and a3 are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set {a2,a3} is a linearly independent set that spans S.

Therefore, a basis of S is {a2,a3}, that is to say,

B={[22]⏟a2,[1−1]⏟a3}.

q-74973.name: Question 3
q-74973.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ by inspection.
q-74973.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{2}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{2}=2\cdot {a}_{1}+0\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{2}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is spanned by just $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}},{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}\}.

Question 3
?

Consider the vectors a1=[−10],a2=[−20], and a3=[−11]. Find a basis of S=Span{a1,a2,a3} by inspection.

a
B={[−11]}
b
B={[−20]}
c
B={[−10],[−20]}
d
B={[−10],[−11]}
e
B={[−10],[−20],[−11]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that a basis of S is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans S.

From the given vectors, we can see that a2 is a linear combination of vectors a1 and a3:

a2=2⋅a1+0⋅a3

Consequently, the vector a2 can be removed from Span{a1,a2,a3} without changing the span. So S=Span{a1,a2,a3} is spanned by just {a1,a3}.

Lastly, note that a1 and a3 are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set {a1,a3} is a linearly independent set that spans S.

Therefore, a basis of S is {a1,a3}, that is to say,

B={[−10]⏟a1,[−11]⏟a3}.

q-110757.name: Question 4
q-110757.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$  by inspection.
q-110757.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{2}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{2}=-3\cdot {a}_{1}+0\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{2}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is spanned by just $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}},{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}\}.
$$

Question 4

Consider the vectors a1=[01],a2=[0−3], and a3=[1−2]. Find a basis of S=Span{a1,a2,a3} by inspection.

a
 B={[01],[0−3],[1−2]}
b
 B={[01],[1−2]}
c
 B={[01],}
d
 B={[01],[0−3]}
e
 B={[1−2]}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Remember that a basis of S is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans S.

From the given vectors, we can see that a2 is a linear combination of vectors a1 and a3:

a2=−3⋅a1+0⋅a3

Consequently, the vector a2 can be removed from Span{a1,a2,a3} without changing the span. So S=Span{a1,a2,a3} is spanned by just {a1,a3}.

Lastly, note that a1 and a3 are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set {a1,a3} is a linearly independent set that spans S.

Therefore, a basis of S is {a1,a3}, that is to say,

B={[01]⏟a1,[1−2]⏟a3}.

q-110752.name: Question 5
q-110752.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ by inspection.
q-110752.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{1}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{1}=1\cdot {a}_{2}+1\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{1}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is spanned by just $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}},{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}\}.
$$

q-110752.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the vectors a1=[5−1],a2=[21], and a3=[3−2]. Find a basis of S=Span{a1,a2,a3} by inspection.

a
 B={[5−1],[21],[3−2]}
b
 B={[21]}
c
 B={[21],[3−2]}
d
 B={[3−2]}
e
 B={[5−1]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that a basis of S is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans S.

From the given vectors, we can see that a1 is a linear combination of vectors a2 and a3:

a1=1⋅a2+1⋅a3

Consequently, the vector a1 can be removed from Span{a1,a2,a3} without changing the span. So S=Span{a1,a2,a3} is spanned by just {a2,a3}.

Lastly, note that a2 and a3 are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set {a2,a3} is a linearly independent set that spans S.

Therefore, a basis of S is {a2,a3}, that is to say,

B={[21]⏟a2,[3−2]⏟a3}.

q-34464.name: Question 6
q-34464.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -14 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
q-34464.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, our matrix is already in a row echelon form.

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Consider the vectors a1=[500], a2=[−170], and a3=[2−140]. Find a basis B of Span{a1,a2,a3}.

a
B={[500],[−170]}
b
B={[500]}
c
B={[−170],[2−140]}
d
B={[−170]}
e
B={[2−140]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

M=[5−1207−14000]

In this case, our matrix is already in a row echelon form.

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 2nd columns are pivot columns, while the 3rd column is a non-pivot column.

The 1st and 2nd columns from the original matrix are a1 and a2. So, a basis of S is {a1,a2}, that is to say,

B={[500],[−170]}.

q-75067.name: Question 7
q-75067.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
q-75067.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ -2 & -1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{3}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Question 7

Consider the vectors a1=[4−2], a2=[2−1], and a3=[67]. Find a basis B of Span{a1,a2,a3}.

a
B={[2−1]}
b
B={[4−2],[2−1]}
c
B={[67]}
d
B={[4−2]}
e
B={[4−2],[67]}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

A=[426−2−17]R2:=R2+12R1∼[4260010]

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 3rd columns are pivot columns, while the 2nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the original matrix, not from the reduced one.

The 1st and 3rd columns from the original matrix are a1 and a3. So, a basis of S is {a1,a3}, that is to say,

B={[4−2],[67]}.
